questions.q: A financial firm must keep backups for 7 years so that no one, including the root user and AWS, can delete them or shorten retention. Which AWS Backup setting meets this?

options.t: Vault access policy that denies backup:DeleteRecoveryPoint
options.why: Wrong: an admin can edit or remove an access policy, so it is not immutable.

options.t: Vault Lock in governance mode
options.why: Wrong: users with backup:DeleteBackupVaultLockConfiguration can change or remove it.

options.t: Vault Lock in compliance mode with ChangeableForDays
options.why: Right: after the grace time (minimum 3 days) the lock is immutable for everyone while recovery points exist.

options.t: S3 Glacier Vault Lock
options.why: Wrong: it locks Glacier vault archives and is unrelated to AWS Backup recovery points.

questions.explain: Only compliance-mode Vault Lock is immutable after its grace time.
questions.remember: Immutable, nobody can remove, regulatory WORM → Vault Lock compliance mode (ChangeableForDays set). Governance mode can be changed by permitted users.
variants: Authorized admins must still be able to remove the lock → governance mode (omit ChangeableForDays).
Locking source S3 objects in a live bucket → S3 Object Lock.
Just blocking deletes with an exception for a break-glass role → vault access policy.

questions.q: A security team wants backups that survive a compromise of the production account, and a separate recovery account must be able to restore them quickly. What should they use?

options.t: A standard vault with a vault access policy
options.why: Wrong: it stays in the compromised account and policies can be changed.

options.t: A logically air-gapped vault shared through AWS RAM
options.why: Right: it is always compliance-locked and can be shared so another account can view and restore.

options.t: Cross-Region copy to a standard vault in the same account
options.why: Wrong: same account, so compromised credentials can still reach it.

options.t: S3 Replication of the backup bucket
options.why: Wrong: replication is not AWS Backup and gives no isolated, locked recovery vault.

questions.explain: LAG vault = compliance lock plus cross-account sharing for recovery.
questions.remember: Recover after account or credential compromise → logically air-gapped vault shared via RAM. Vault Lock alone only protects inside your own account.
variants: Only need WORM inside the same account → Vault Lock compliance mode.
Share to a whole organization or OU → not possible, RAM sharing is per account ID only.
Shared account wants to copy backups out → not allowed, the owning account makes copies.

questions.q: An S3 bucket must be restorable to any second within the last 14 days, plus monthly backups kept for 5 years. Which design works?

options.t: One rule with continuous backup and 5-year retention
options.why: Wrong: continuous backup retention is 1 to 35 days only.

options.t: One continuous rule (up to 35 days) plus a monthly snapshot rule with long retention
options.why: Right: PITR covers the short window and the snapshot rule covers long retention. Versioning must be on.

options.t: A daily snapshot rule only
options.why: Wrong: snapshots give no restore to an arbitrary second.

options.t: A continuous rule with cold storage after 30 days
options.why: Wrong: S3 backups do not support cold storage and continuous cannot exceed 35 days.

questions.explain: Pair a continuous rule with a snapshot rule.
questions.remember: PITR needs continuous backup, max 35 days; long retention needs snapshot rules (up to 100 years). S3 needs versioning.
variants: RDS instance instead of S3 → same pattern, continuous is supported.
RDS Multi-AZ DB cluster → continuous not supported.
DynamoDB PITR → native feature, 1 to 35 days.

questions.q: A backup rule transitions recovery points to cold storage after 30 days and deletes them after 90 days. The save is rejected. What is the problem?

options.t: Nothing, it is valid
options.why: Wrong: cold storage needs a 90-day minimum stay.

options.t: DeleteAfterDays must be at least MoveToColdStorageAfterDays plus 90
options.why: Right: 30 + 90 = 120, so 90 days is invalid.

options.t: Cold storage requires 60 days in warm first
options.why: Wrong: the notes do not state a 60-day warm minimum for cold storage.

options.t: Cold storage cannot be used with EFS
options.why: Wrong: EFS supports cold storage.

questions.explain: Cold storage minimum stay is 90 days.
questions.remember: DeleteAfterDays ≥ MoveToColdStorageAfterDays + 90. Once in cold it cannot move back.
variants: Transition 10 days, delete 100 days → valid.
RDS or S3 backups → cannot use cold storage at all.
EBS cold → needs opt-in and a monthly or less frequent schedule.

questions.q: A company must copy backups from many workload accounts to one central backup account in the same organization. Which items are required? (Choose 3)

options.t: Cross-account backup turned on in the management account's AWS Backup settings
options.why: Right: it is required for cross-account copy.

options.t: Destination vault access policy allowing backup:CopyIntoBackupVault
options.why: Right: the destination must permit the copy.

options.t: A customer managed KMS key for non-fully-managed types, granted to the destination
options.why: Right: AWS managed keys cannot be shared across accounts.

options.t: VPC peering between the accounts
options.why: Wrong: AWS Backup copies do not use customer networking.

options.t: An AWS Backup gateway in each account
options.why: Wrong: the gateway is for on-premises and VMware workloads.

questions.explain: Org setting, destination vault policy and a shareable CMK.
questions.remember: Cross-account copy: same organization, cross-account backup enabled, destination vault policy, CMK for non-fully-managed types.
variants: Copying to another Region in the same account → a copy action, no org setting needed.
Redshift or standard DynamoDB → no copy at all.
Destination is a LAG vault → copy is encrypted per vault, other types need a CMK.

questions.q: A data sovereignty rule says no backup or copy may ever exist outside eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. What is the most reliable control?

options.t: Tell teams not to add copy actions
options.why: Wrong: a process rule can be bypassed.

options.t: An SCP that denies backup actions when aws:RequestedRegion is not in the approved list
options.why: Right: it enforces the Region limit organization-wide, exempting global services.

options.t: A vault access policy on the Default vault
options.why: Wrong: it covers one vault, not new vaults in other Regions.

options.t: Backup Audit Manager report plans
options.why: Wrong: reports detect after the fact and do not prevent.

questions.explain: SCP Region deny is the preventive control.
questions.remember: Prevent backups or copies in disallowed Regions → SCP with aws:RequestedRegion. SCPs do not apply to the management account.
variants: Detect rather than prevent → Audit Manager cross-Region control or Config.
Restrict who deletes recovery points → SCP deny on backup:DeleteRecoveryPoint.
Management account workloads → SCP does not cover them.

questions.q: A platform team needs every new account in an organization to get the same baseline backup plan without logging in to the account. What should they use?

options.t: An AWS Backup policy attached to the root or OU
options.why: Right: the effective policy creates an organization-managed plan in each member account.

options.t: Manual plans in each account
options.why: Wrong: no consistency guarantee.

options.t: Cross-account monitoring
options.why: Wrong: it only shows jobs, it does not deploy plans.

options.t: A logically air-gapped vault
options.why: Wrong: it stores copies, it does not deploy plans.

questions.explain: Organizations backup policies deploy plans centrally.
questions.remember: Central baseline plans for all accounts → Organizations backup policy; the target vault and IAM role must already exist in each member account (StackSets). Resources are selected by tag.
variants: Only see jobs across accounts → cross-account monitoring.
Keep daily operations out of the management account → delegated administrator.
Member wants to edit the plan → cannot, it is organization-managed.

questions.q: A tag-based assignment is meant to protect resources tagged Backup=daily AND Env=prod, but resources with only Backup=daily are also being backed up. What is the likely cause?

options.t: The tags were put in ListOfTags, where any matching tag is included (OR)
options.why: Right: ListOfTags is OR; Conditions are evaluated as AND.

options.t: The plan has too many rules
options.why: Wrong: rule count does not affect selection.

options.t: The vault has no KMS key
options.why: Wrong: every vault has a key and it is unrelated to selection.

options.t: Service opt-in is off
options.why: Wrong: that would skip resources, not include extra ones.

questions.remember: Need all tags to match → use Conditions (AND). ListOfTags matches any tag (OR).
variants: Resource not backed up at all → check service opt-in per Region.
Exclude scratch volumes → NotResources.
Resource assignment IAM role → needs iam:PassRole for the caller.

questions.q: A backup job for an RDS instance has status EXPIRED every night. The start window is 1 hour and the job is scheduled during the database's maintenance window. What is the best fix?

options.t: Lengthen the completion window
options.why: Wrong: the completion window applies after the job starts; this job never started.

options.t: Move the schedule away from the maintenance window and widen the start window
options.why: Right: databases cannot start a backup during or 1 hour before maintenance, so the job never starts inside the start window.

options.t: Switch to cold storage
options.why: Wrong: RDS does not support cold storage and it is unrelated.

options.t: Run two concurrent jobs on the instance
options.why: Wrong: only 1 concurrent job per resource is allowed.

questions.explain: EXPIRED = never started inside the start window.
questions.remember: EXPIRED → never started in the start window; cancelled → started but missed the completion window. Avoid maintenance windows (Aurora is exempt).
variants: Job started but ran too long → completion window (does not apply to FSx).
FSx → cannot start 3 hours before maintenance or backup window.
Aurora → exempt from the maintenance window restriction.

questions.q: An operations team wants an alert only when AWS Backup jobs fail, with a metric they can alarm on and automated ticket creation. Which combination fits?

options.t: CloudWatch metric NumberOfBackupJobsFailed with an alarm, and an EventBridge rule on Backup Job State Change
options.why: Right: metrics drive alarms, EventBridge events (source aws.backup) trigger automation.

options.t: Vault SNS notifications on BACKUP_JOB_COMPLETED only, unfiltered
options.why: Wrong: that event fires for success and failure, so it is noisy.

options.t: CloudTrail data events
options.why: Wrong: CloudTrail records API calls, not job outcomes.

options.t: Audit Manager framework only
options.why: Wrong: it reports compliance on a 24 h or config-change cycle, not job alerts.

questions.explain: Metrics plus EventBridge for job failure alerting.
questions.remember: Alert and automate on failed jobs → CloudWatch AWS/Backup metrics and alarms, EventBridge aws.backup events. SNS BACKUP_JOB_COMPLETED needs a state filter.
variants: Who deleted a recovery point → CloudTrail.
Prove policy compliance → Backup Audit Manager with AWS Config recording.
Notify per vault → vault SNS topic, one per vault.
